result.question: How does Nvidia describe competition for its data center products?
result.answer: Nvidia describes competition for its data center products in the risk factors section of its fiscal 2026 first-quarter 10-Q, under the heading "Competition could adversely impact our market share and financial results." The company states that its target markets remain competitive and that competition may intensify with expanding and changing product and service offerings, industry standards, customer and market needs, new entrants, and consolidations [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. Competitors compete on a wide range of parameters including price, total cost of ownership, and performance, which has resulted and may in the future result in lower-than-expected selling prices or demand for Nvidia's products [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. Some competitors operate their own fabrication facilities and have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios and patent protections, more design wins, and greater financial, sales, marketing, and distribution resources than Nvidia, and may acquire market share, capitalize on new market opportunities more effectively, transition products more quickly, and impinge on Nvidia's ability to procure sufficient foundry capacity and scarce input materials during a supply-constrained environment [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. With respect to data center systems specifically, Nvidia notes that some of its customers are developing their own ASICs and other products, including designs optimized for certain workloads that may not require all of the features and functionality Nvidia's data center systems provide [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. The company also states that others may offer cloud-based services that compete with its AI cloud service offerings, and that it may not be able to establish market share sufficient to achieve the scale necessary to meet its business objectives [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. If Nvidia is unable to successfully compete in this environment, demand for its products, services, and technologies could decrease, which may negatively impact its business [0001045810-26-000052:part-ii--item-1a-p001]. The fiscal 2026 10-K similarly describes competition under the same heading, noting that competitors' products, services, and technologies may be cheaper or provide better functionality or features than Nvidia's, and that some customers have in-house expertise and internal development capabilities and can use or develop their own solutions to replace those Nvidia is providing [0001045810-26-000021:item-1a-p004].
